reasons: The declared independent-unit column is log_id, and the frozen data/input.csv contains 20 rows with 20 distinct log_id values (OG-01..OG-10, SG-01..SG-10); no identifier repeats, so no independent unit appears in more than one row.

Both arms of the procedure are covered: the contingency() function tallies exactly one count per row into the old_growth arm (10 rows) and the second_growth arm (10 rows), and read_logs() raises an error if any log_id repeats, so each arm's cell counts are built from distinct independent units and the marginals (10 and 10) match the row counts per stand.

The selected report demonstrates the absence of the issue: it identifies the unit ('One row per surveyed log (log_id), 20 logs in total, each from its own survey site and inspected exactly once'), states in the Analysis section that each of the 20 rows contributes one independent observation, and states in the Interpretation that the 20 rows are the 20 independent units with no unit represented more than once; the printed contingency table [[9, 1], [2, 8]] sums to 20, consistent with one entry per unique log_id in the frozen data.

The reported figures are reproducible from the frozen data: 9 of 10 old-growth and 2 of 10 second-growth logs have fruiting_bodies_present = 1, giving sample odds ratio (9*8)/(1*2) = 36.00 and a two-sided Fisher's exact p of about 0.005477, matching the [selected-result] line.

Declared independent unit mussel_id is consistent with the frozen data: exactly 12 tag codes (MU-01 to MU-12), each appearing 6 times with session_no 1-6, constant shell_length_mm within each mussel, and each mussel contributing 3 pre and 3 post runs, so both arms of the paired comparison (pre vs post phase) draw on the same 12 independent animals rather than on independent groups of rows.

The selected report demonstrates absence of the row-independence violation: it explicitly states the 72 run rows are not 72 independent observations, describes collapsing runs to one pre mean and one post mean per mussel_id, and applies a paired t-test to the 12 within-animal changes.

The reported degrees of freedom, t(11), match n = 12 independent units minus one, not the 72 raw rows (which would have produced df of 70 or 71 under a row-level analysis), confirming the test was run on the collapsed per-animal table.

Recomputation from data/input.csv verifies the report's numbers: all 12 per-animal pre/post means and changes match (e.g., MU-01 pre 3.400, post 2.500, change -0.900), mean change -0.917 L/h, SD 0.212, SE 0.0613, t = -14.944 on 11 df, and 95% CI -1.052 to -0.782 using t_crit(11) = 2.201; the workflow code performs exactly the collapse the report describes.
No authority lock was minted, so lock conformance to the declaration cannot be assessed; the answer is not-applicable-no-lock.

The declared independent-unit column collar_id matches the frozen data: exactly 12 distinct collars (D01-D06, N01-N06), each appearing exactly 5 times, and peat_condition is constant within every collar in both arms, so the treatment is fixed at the collar level as declared.

The selected report demonstrates the issue: it states 'Every chamber closure in data/input.csv is entered as one observation', reports n = 30 per arm and Welch df = 57.55, i.e. 60 rows treated as independent in a row-independent two-sample t-test, although only 12 independent collars exist and each contributes 5 repeated visits. This is pseudoreplication entered directly into the procedure.

The lock's authorization does not follow from the declaration alone. The declaration establishes collar_id as the independent unit with 5 dependent rows per collar; from that alone, a row-level scipy.stats.ttest_ind over all 60 closures cannot be dependence-free. The lock nonetheless marks authority_state 'authorized' with authorized_key_columns ['collar_id'] for exactly that row-level procedure, so the authorization contradicts rather than follows from the declaration; collar_id also does not uniquely key the rows the procedure actually consumes (collar_id + closure_index does).

The lock's own limitations concede it establishes no numerical impact or scientific correctness, and its approval timestamp (2026-08-15) postdates the current date, further undermining any claim that the declaration alone licenses the minted authorization.

Declaration consistency: the declared independent-unit column vessel_id matches the frozen data. There are exactly 8 vessels (V01-V08), each appearing in exactly 4 rows (one per sample_point p1-p4), for 32 data rows. Each vessel maps to exactly one procedure arm: V01-V04 are all rye, V05-V08 are all wheat, so 4 independent units per arm with no vessel straddling arms. The declaration 'one row = one reading at one location inside one vessel; independent unit = vessel_id' is fully consistent with the data.

Issue demonstrated in the selected report: the report itself states 'Each vessel was sampled at four separate points in the dough, and every reading enters the comparison as one observation,' and its summary table shows 4 vessels but 16 readings per arm. The selected result runs a Mann-Whitney U test on 16 vs 16 readings with an exact null over C(32,16)=601,080,390 rank assignments, treating all 32 rows as exchangeable independent observations. Mann-Whitney is a row-independent procedure; the exact permutation null it computes assumes each reading is an independent unit. Feeding 4 repeated within-vessel measurements per vessel as separate rows is exactly the flagged issue, and it is demonstrated on the face of the report (vessel counts vs reading counts, the 16-vs-16 sample sizes, and the 601M-arrangement null are all printed). The true independent sample size is 4 vs 4 vessels; the reported p = 3.327e-09 is only attainable by inflating n via pseudoreplication (a 4-vs-4 exact test's minimum two-sided p is 2/70 ≈ 0.029).

Lock follows declaration: a lock is present with authorized_key_columns = ['vessel_id'], which is exactly the declared independent-unit column from the data description, for the same input path and procedure (scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu). The key authorization therefore follows from the declaration alone. Note the lock, by its own stated limitations, authorizes only the unit key; it does not certify that the analysis actually aggregated to or grouped by vessel_id, and the workflow does not — it never uses vessel_id in the test, only for the display count of vessels.

Declaration check: data-description.md declares terrace_id as the independent unit column, and the frozen data/input.csv is consistent with this in both procedure arms — each of TR-01..TR-05 (biochar arm) and TR-06..TR-10 (none arm) appears exactly four times, once per plot P1..P4, and treatment is constant within every terrace, confirming terrace-level treatment assignment and four repeated measurements per independent unit in each arm.

Selected report check: the report itself demonstrates the issue. Its Question section states four sampling plots were read on every terrace, and its Analysis section states 'Each of the 40 plot measurements was entered as one observation' into a Welch two-sample t-test (scipy.stats.ttest_ind, a row-independent procedure). The [selected-result] line confirms n = 40 with df = 35.31, i.e., the t-test treated 40 clustered plot readings as independent when only 10 terraces (5 per arm) are independent units. Repeated measurements from the same independent unit were entered into a row-independent procedure as if independent, and this is visible on the face of the selected report, so the demonstration is 'issue'.

No aggregation to terrace level (e.g., terrace means giving n = 5 per arm, df ≈ 8) appears anywhere in the workflow or report; the workflow filters rows by treatment and passes all plot rows directly to ttest_ind, matching the report's description.

Lock check: a lock was minted (lock_kind dependence_method_authorization_v1). Its human_method_authorization record lists authorized_key_columns = ['terrace_id'], which is exactly the independent unit column stated in the declaration, for the same input path and the same procedure (scipy.stats.ttest_ind).
